title: Extremal spectral gap of regular graphs with bounded vertex connectivity
summary: The well-known inequality of Fiedler ensures that the spectral gap $r-λ_2(G)$ of a connected non-complete $r$-regular graph $G$ is bounded from above by the vertex connectivity $κ(G)$ of $G$. We prove that, for integers $t\geq2$ and $r>2t^2$, every connected $r$-regular graph with vertex connectivity at most $2t$ has spectral gap at most $\frac{1}{2}(r+t+2-\sqrt{(r-t+2)^2-4t(t-1)})$. We show that this bound is nearly optimal for each fixed $t \ge 2$ and sufficiently large $r > 2t^2$ such that $r+1$ is divisible by $t$.
